title: Drone lessons for North Korea from Russia's war in Ukraine | The Impossible State
summary: CSIS Korea podcast on drone lessons from Ukraine: North Korean troops gaining combat experience, cheap drone swarms beating costly air defences, and escalation risk on the peninsula.

assertions.quote: North Korea sent troops, right? Uh to fight for Russia in Ukraine in the Kursk region.
learn lessons that then North Korea can apply towards any kind of attacks or or skirmishes on the Korean Peninsula

verdicts.note: Reports show North Korean units adapted to drone warfare in Kursk, and returning troops carry that experience home.
US intelligence says North Korean troops are gaining valuable warfighting experience in Ukraine as a spillover of the war; its use on the peninsula is implied, not stated.
The monitoring team says North Korea gains first-hand experience in modern warfare from its troops' support of Russia against Ukraine, but does not say how it could be used on the Korean peninsula.

assertions.quote: you send enough of them and it overwhelms even the sophisticated air defense and missile defense systems

verdicts.note: In Ukraine, mass drone attacks saturate and exhaust air defences at far lower cost than the interceptors.
US intelligence says rivals plan to use cheap expendable systems alongside missiles to stress US defences; stressing is not shown to mean overwhelming.

assertions.quote: now they start to replace and substitute conventional weapon systems such as missiles, for example.

verdicts.note: Drones now cause most front-line casualties in Ukraine, but artillery, missiles and armour still play major roles.
US intelligence says that despite the spread of one-way attack drones, rival militaries will keep prioritising advanced missiles and pair them with cheap drones rather than replace them.

assertions.quote: you could have very quickly escalation either inadvertent or sort of a tit-for-tat escalation that leads to a more strategic conflict.

verdicts.note: Past incidents (the 2015 shelling, the 2022-24 drone incursions) did not escalate; the risk is real but small.

assertions.quote: it's a very high percentage of our high-value offensive and defensive missiles.
They have, you know, hypervelocity uh maneuverable warheads that can evade allied missile defenses.

verdicts.note: North Korea has tested hypersonic and manoeuvring missiles, but how well they defeat defences is unproven.
SIPRI reports North Korea unveiled and tested new systems in 2025, including the solid-fuelled Hwasong-20 ICBM and highly manoeuvrable medium-range systems designed to evade missile defences.
US intelligence says North Korea, with China, Russia and Pakistan, is fielding delivery systems with more range and accuracy designed to challenge US and regional missile defences.
